# Instructions 

1. Save/open this script as UTF-8. Requires only base R.

2. Download the Hungarian TEXT vectors (cc.hu.300.vec.gz):
https://dl.fbaipublicfiles.com/fasttext/vectors-crawl/cc.hu.300.vec.gz

3. Set SETTINGS$model_file below. No extraction is necessary.

4. Run the whole script with RStudio's Source button.

# Information

Model: fastText, Hungarian Common Crawl + Wikipedia, 300 dimensions.
Documentation: https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/crawl-vectors.html
Citation: Grave, Bojanowski, Gupta, Joulin, & Mikolov (2018).
Learning Word Vectors for 157 Languages. LREC.
Model license: CC BY-SA 3.0.

The words here are a project-specific, non-normed candidate pool. The words were AI generated or added randomly. Familiarity/concreteness/neutrality were qualitative selection intentions, not measured or matched properties. No cosine values are invented.

# Settings

```{r}
SETTINGS <- list(
  # change this to your path
  model_file = "C:/Users/Acer/Downloads/cc.hu.300.vec.gz", 
  # output directory for the results (will be created if it doesn't exist)
  output_dir = file.path(getwd(), "wordpair_cosine_results"),
  # number of word pairs to process in one chunk (to avoid memory issues)
  chunk_size = 5000L 
)
```

# Word pool

```{r}
word_pool <- data.frame(
  # Create a unique word ID for each word
  word_id = sprintf(
    "word_%02d", seq_along(c(original_words, additional_words))
  ),
  # Combine the original and additional words into a single vector
  word = c(original_words, additional_words),
  # Create a column indicating the origin of each word
  origin = c(
    rep("original", length(original_words)),
    rep("additional_ai_proposed", length(additional_words))
  ),
  # Prevent automatic conversion of strings to factors
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE 
)
```

# Validation of the word pool

Here, we define a function to validate the word pool. The function checks for the following conditions: 
- There must be at least two non-empty, single-word entries.
- There should be no duplicate words or word IDs.
- There should be no overlap with the practice words.

```{r}
validate_pool <- function(pool, excluded_words = practice_words) {    # exclude practice words
  words <- enc2utf8(pool$word)                                        # ensure UTF-8 encoding
  if (length(words) < 2L || anyNA(words) ||                           # if less than 2 words/any NA values
      any(!nzchar(words)) || any(grepl("[[:space:]]", words))) {      # if any words are empty/contain spaces
    stop("Use at least two nonempty, single-word entries.")        
  }
  if (anyDuplicated(words)) {                                         # if there are any duplicated words
    stop("Duplicate words: ", paste(unique(words[duplicated(words)]), 
                                   collapse = ", "))
  }
  if (anyDuplicated(pool$word_id)) stop("Word IDs must be unique.")
  overlap <- intersect(words, excluded_words)
  if (length(overlap)) {
    stop("Practice-word overlap: ", paste(overlap, collapse = ", "))   # if  overlap with practice words
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}
```

# Stream the .vec/.vec.gz file in chunks and retain only requested vectors.

Unlike loading the entire model, this does not require its full size in RAM. Text vectors cannot generate vectors for out-of-vocabulary words.

```{r}
read_selected_vectors <- function(model_file, words, chunk_size = 5000L) {
  if (!file.exists(model_file)) {
    stop(
      "Model file not found: ", model_file,
      "\nDownload cc.hu.300.vec.gz and update SETTINGS$model_file.",
      "\nUse the TEXT (.vec.gz) download, not the binary (.bin.gz) model."
    )
  }
  if (length(chunk_size) != 1L || is.na(chunk_size) ||
      chunk_size < 1L || chunk_size != as.integer(chunk_size)) {
    stop("chunk_size must be a positive integer.")
  }

  # Mark input as UTF-8 in readLines instead of converting it to the native
  # Windows locale, which may not be able to represent Hungarian accents.
  connection <- if (grepl("\\.gz$", model_file, ignore.case = TRUE)) {
    gzfile(model_file, open = "rt")
  } else {
    file(model_file, open = "rt")
  }
  on.exit(close(connection), add = TRUE)

  first_line <- readLines(connection, n = 1L, warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
  if (!length(first_line)) stop("The model file is empty.")
  first_line <- sub("^\ufeff", "", first_line)
  header <- strsplit(trimws(first_line), "[[:space:]]+")[[1L]]
  if (length(header) != 2L || !all(grepl("^[0-9]+$", header))) {
    stop("Expected a text-vector header: vocabulary_size dimensions.")
  }
  vocabulary_size <- as.numeric(header[1L])
  dimensions <- as.integer(header[2L])
  if (!is.finite(vocabulary_size) || vocabulary_size < 1 ||
      is.na(dimensions) || dimensions < 1L) {
    stop("Invalid model dimensions or vocabulary size.")
  }

  vectors <- matrix(
    NA_real_, nrow = length(words), ncol = dimensions,
    dimnames = list(words, paste0("dim_", seq_len(dimensions)))
  )
  found <- rep(FALSE, length(words))
  scanned <- 0
  next_progress <- 100000

  repeat {
    lines <- readLines(connection, n = chunk_size, warn = FALSE,
                       encoding = "UTF-8")
    if (!length(lines)) break
    scanned <- scanned + length(lines)

    # Identify the first token without splitting every full vector.
    separators <- regexpr("[ \t]", lines)
    tokens <- substring(lines, 1L, pmax(0L, separators - 1L))
    indices <- match(tokens, words)
    matches <- which(!is.na(indices))

    for (line_number in matches) {
      word_number <- indices[line_number]
      if (found[word_number]) next
      vector_text <- substring(lines[line_number],
                               separators[line_number] + 1L)
      values <- scan(text = vector_text, what = double(), quiet = TRUE)
      if (length(values) != dimensions || any(!is.finite(values))) {
        stop("Invalid vector for word: ", words[word_number])
      }
      vectors[word_number, ] <- values
      found[word_number] <- TRUE
    }

    if (all(found)) break
    if (scanned >= next_progress) {
      message("Scanned ", scanned, " rows; found ",
              sum(found), "/", length(words), " words.")
      next_progress <- scanned + 100000
    }
  }

  if (!all(found)) {
    stop(
      "Missing words in the model: ",
      paste(words[!found], collapse = ", "),
      "\nNo scores were substituted and no words were silently dropped.",
      "\nCheck spelling, UTF-8 encoding, model choice, and download completeness."
    )
  }
  list(vectors = vectors, vocabulary_size = vocabulary_size,
       dimensions = dimensions)
}
```


# Calculating pairwise cosine similarities

Here, we define a function to calculate pairwise cosine similarities for all unordered combinations of words in the pool. The function checks for valid input and computes the cosine similarity using normalized vectors.

```{r}
calculate_all_pairs <- function(vectors, pool) {
  validate_pool(pool)
  if (!identical(rownames(vectors), pool$word)) {
    stop("The vector rows and word-pool order do not match.")
  }
  if (any(!is.finite(vectors))) stop("Non-finite vector values.")
  norms <- sqrt(rowSums(vectors^2))
  if (any(!is.finite(norms) | norms == 0)) {
    stop("Cannot compute cosine for a zero-length or invalid vector.")
  }

  unit_vectors <- sweep(vectors, 1L, norms, "/")
  similarities <- tcrossprod(unit_vectors)
  # Correct only floating-point overshoot at -1/+1.
  similarities[] <- pmax(-1, pmin(1, similarities))

  # Unordered combinations: A-B once, no B-A duplicate, no A-A comparison.
  combinations <- t(combn(seq_len(nrow(pool)), 2L))
  result <- data.frame(
    combination_id = sprintf("combination_%04d", seq_len(nrow(combinations))),
    word_1_id = pool$word_id[combinations[, 1L]],
    word_1 = pool$word[combinations[, 1L]],
    word_2_id = pool$word_id[combinations[, 2L]],
    word_2 = pool$word[combinations[, 2L]],
    cosine_similarity = similarities[combinations],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  stopifnot(nrow(result) == choose(nrow(pool), 2L))
  result <- result[order(-result$cosine_similarity,
                         result$word_1_id, result$word_2_id), ]
  rownames(result) <- NULL
  result
}
```

# Run analyses

Here, we define a function to run the analysis. It reads the word vectors, calculates pairwise cosine similarities, and saves the results to an output directory. The function also ensures that the R session is using a UTF-8 locale to handle accented words correctly.

```{r}
run_analysis <- function(model_file, output_dir, pool = word_pool,
                         chunk_size = SETTINGS$chunk_size) {
  # Older/non-UTF-8 sessions can write literal "<U+...>" escapes into a CSV.
  # Use a UTF-8 character locale for this run, then restore the user's locale.
  if (!isTRUE(l10n_info()[["UTF-8"]])) {
    previous_locale <- Sys.getlocale("LC_CTYPE")
    on.exit(suppressWarnings(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", previous_locale)),
            add = TRUE)
    utf8_locale <- if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
      "English_United States.utf8"
    } else {
      "C.UTF-8"
    }
    suppressWarnings(Sys.setlocale("LC_CTYPE", utf8_locale))
    if (!isTRUE(l10n_info()[["UTF-8"]])) {
      stop("A UTF-8-capable R session is required to export accented words.")
    }
  }
  validate_pool(pool)
  message("Words: ", nrow(pool), "; combinations: ", choose(nrow(pool), 2L))
  message("Reading word vectors. The full model is not loaded into memory.")
  model <- read_selected_vectors(model_file, pool$word, chunk_size)
  pairs <- calculate_all_pairs(model$vectors, pool)

  # A new run directory prevents previous results from being overwritten.
  dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  run_dir <- tempfile(
    pattern = paste0("run_", format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%d_%H%M%S"), "_"),
    tmpdir = output_dir
  )
  if (!dir.create(run_dir)) stop("Could not create the results directory.")

  write.csv(pool, file.path(run_dir, "word_pool.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
  write.csv(pairs, file.path(run_dir, "all_pair_cosines.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")

  # Preserve the actual vectors used, not just their derived similarities.
  saveRDS(model$vectors, file.path(run_dir, "selected_word_vectors.rds"))
  writeLines(c(
    "Model intended by this script: fastText cc.hu.300, Common Crawl + Wikipedia",
    "Source: https://fasttext.cc/docs/en/crawl-vectors.html",
    "Download: https://dl.fbaipublicfiles.com/fasttext/vectors-crawl/cc.hu.300.vec.gz",
    "License: CC BY-SA 3.0",
    "Citation: Grave et al. (2018), Learning Word Vectors for 157 Languages, LREC.",
    paste("Actual local model path:", normalizePath(model_file, winslash = "/")),
    paste("Model file size (bytes):", file.info(model_file)$size),
    paste("Dimensions read from file:", model$dimensions),
    paste("Vocabulary size in header:", model$vocabulary_size),
    paste("Run time UTC:", format(Sys.time(), tz = "UTC", usetz = TRUE)),
    paste("Number of words:", nrow(pool)),
    paste("Number of unordered pairs:", nrow(pairs)),
    "Measure: cosine similarity, not cosine distance.",
    "No cosine filtering, rounding, pairing assignment, or random sampling applied.",
    "word_1/word_2 identify an unordered pair, not assigned cue/target roles.",
    "Original 40 words: user-provided materials.",
    "Additional 40 words: OpenAI AI assistant's qualitative suggestions.",
    "No normative matching or empirical validation of the word pool.",
    "These are not the original SPAML stimuli or SPAML cosine values.",
    "If another model was used, replace the intended-model attribution above.",
    "",
    capture.output(sessionInfo())
  ), file.path(run_dir, "analysis_info.txt"), useBytes = TRUE)

  message("Complete. Output folder: ", normalizePath(run_dir, winslash = "/"))
  print(utils::head(pairs, 10L), row.names = FALSE)
  invisible(list(pairs = pairs, words = pool, vectors = model$vectors,
                 output_dir = normalizePath(run_dir, winslash = "/")))
}

```

# Save the results of the analysis and filter for candidate pairs with cosine similarity between 0.15 and 0.30.

```{r}
results <- run_analysis(SETTINGS$model_file, SETTINGS$output_dir)

candidates <- subset(
  results$pairs,
  cosine_similarity >= 0.15 & cosine_similarity <= 0.30
)

candidates |> knitr::kable(
  caption = "Candidate word pairs with cosine similarity between 0.15 and 0.30",
  digits = 3
)
```

# Results

Results go to folder `wordpair_cosine_results` in the current working directory. Each run creates a new subfolder with the following files:

- `all_pair_cosines.csv`: all combinations, decreasing cosine similarity
- `word_pool.csv`: 100 words with IDs and origin labels
- `selected_word_vectors.rds`: used vectors for the 100 words, in a matrix with rownames
- `analysis_info.txt`: details of the run, including model path, size, dimensions, and session info
